$comment: R1840 — THE OPTION SURFACE THE TOOL IS AN EDITOR FOR, SOURCED RATHER THAN
DECLARED.
R1690 built `hello-node-lab::settings::schema` and registered the defect in
the same breath: the surface the reach meter divides by was written BY HAND
IN THE SAME CRATE AS THE SCREEN UNDER TEST. That is the shape the sibling
specification pins already refuse (`ls docs/analyzer-*-spec.json`, and ask
the directory rather than trusting a number written here — the first draft
of this line said THREE and there were twelve) — a specification written by the same
hand in the same edit as its subject means a conformance check is asking the
subject for the answer — and the coverage meter made it worse than usual,
because the drift has a DIRECTION: a surface that falls behind its target
shrinks the denominator, so the number goes UP. Drift reads as progress.
This file is that surface, taken from outside the crate.
EXTRACTION. The behaviour reference is not in this repository and must not
be. Its node inspector declares each row as a typed descriptor whose key is
the target's configuration path VERBATIM, and marks the rows that are NOT
configuration paths with a scope word of its own — traffic parameters and
placement axes that have no key in the target. So the split below is the
reference's own, read off its data, not a judgement made here. Measured
2026-08-26: 53 configuration paths and 23 declared not-configuration.
THE DERIVATION POINT, which is the half R1690 said was missing. The
reference does not merely list paths — it CITES the target's own default
configuration document by line range, ten times, beside the fields those
lines authorise. So this surface is two derivations deep and both are
recorded: the target declares it, the reference read the target and says
where, and this file read the reference and says when.
WHAT THIS IS NOT. It is not the shapes. The reference's type words are
coarse (`text`, `int`, `enum`, `json`), and this tree's `FieldType` is
finer — a formatted address, a bounded integer, a unique identifier. The
shapes stay the screen's, and are refined per path in `settings.rs`. What
moves here is the POPULATION, which is the thing a meter divides by.

$extracted.from: the behaviour reference's node-inspector field table
$extracted.note: the count above is how many times the reference names a line range of the target's own default configuration document beside the fields it authorises; it is the derivation point, recorded rather than assumed

$substituted.why: the reference's vocabulary is confidential; structure and behaviour are reproduced, words are not
$substituted.how: path stems are substituted one-for-one, following the conventions `settings.rs` already used, so a path here and the same path there differ only in the substituted stem
$substituted.note: the neutral side is recorded and the original side deliberately is not — writing the mapping down here would publish exactly what the substitution exists to withhold

not_config.$why: the reference marks these with a scope word of its own: they are traffic parameters and placement axes with no key in the target. Recorded rather than dropped, because a path missing from the surface and a path the target has no key for are different facts, and a census that could not tell them apart would report the second as a gap forever

$also_a_path.why: the reference's split is per ROW, not per name: a row is configuration or it is not, and the same word can be both on two different rows. `id` is the target's own identity path on an infrastructure row AND the run-only argument a traffic program takes.
